title: Configure Azure Monitor Log Analytics Workspaces and Diagnostic Settings
summary: Deploy a central Log Analytics workspace with custom retention, configure diagnostic settings to stream audit and performance logs, and query with KQL.
scenarioTemplate: Enterprise compliance at {{companyName}} requires centralized observability for cloud resources in '{{region}}'. You are tasked with creating resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provisioning an Azure Log Analytics Workspace named '{{workspaceName}}' with a {{retentionDays}}-day data retention period, configuring Diagnostic Settings on a target resource to export logs and metrics, and executing sample Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Log Analytics Workspace '{{workspaceName}}' with retentionInDays set to {{retentionDays}}.
Deploy a target resource (Storage Account) in '{{resourceGroup}}'.
Configure Diagnostic Settings '{{diagnosticSettingName}}' exporting metrics and logs to '{{workspaceName}}'.
Execute a test KQL query against the workspace and verify log schema readiness.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Log Analytics Workspace
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Log Analytics workspaces** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{workspaceName}}`, Region: `{{region}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**. Once deployed, open `{{workspaceName}}` > **Usage and estimated costs** > **Data Retention** > set to `{{retentionDays}}` days > click **OK**.
steps.validation: az monitor log-analytics workspace show --workspace-name {{workspaceName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, RetentionDays:retentionInDays, State:provisioningState}' -o table

steps.title: Deploy Target Workload Resource
steps.portalGuide: In `{{resourceGroup}}`, create a Storage Account `stmonitor{{rand5}}` with Standard LRS redundancy.
steps.cliCommand:
az storage account create \
  --name stmonitor{{rand5}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2
steps.validation: az storage account show --name stmonitor{{rand5}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'provisioningState' -o tsv

steps.title: Configure Diagnostic Settings Export to Workspace
steps.portalGuide: Open `stmonitor{{rand5}}` > select **Diagnostic settings** (under Monitoring) > **+ Add diagnostic setting**. Name: `{{diagnosticSettingName}}`. Destination: Check **Send to Log Analytics workspace** > select `{{workspaceName}}`. Select **Transaction** metrics > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
WORKSPACE_ID=$(az monitor log-analytics workspace show --workspace-name {{workspaceName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)
ST_ID=$(az storage account show --name stmonitor{{rand5}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)

az monitor diagnostic-settings create \
  --name {{diagnosticSettingName}} \
  --resource "$ST_ID/blobServices/default" \
  --workspace "$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  --metrics '[{"category": "Transaction", "enabled": true}]'
steps.powershellCommand:
$law = Get-AzOperationalInsightsWorkspace -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Name '{{workspaceName}}'
$st = Get-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Name 'stmonitor{{rand5}}'
# Configure diagnostic settings cmdlet
az monitor diagnostic-settings show --name {{diagnosticSettingName}} --resource "$($st.Id)/blobServices/default"
steps.validation: az monitor diagnostic-settings list --resource $(az storage account show --name stmonitor{{rand5}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)/blobServices/default --query "[].{Name:name, Workspace:workspaceId}" -o table

title: Configure Azure Metric Alerts and Multi-Channel Action Groups
summary: Implement proactive incident notification by configuring Action Groups and Azure Metric Alert rules with static evaluation thresholds.
scenarioTemplate: You are establishing operational alert notifications for production workloads in '{{region}}'. Inside resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', create an Action Group named '{{actionGroupName}}' configured to send email notifications to '{{emailAddress}}'. Then create an Azure Metric Alert rule named '{{alertRuleName}}' that evaluates every 5 minutes and fires a Severity {{severity}} alert when average CPU percentage (or storage capacity) exceeds {{thresholdPct}}%.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Create an Action Group named '{{actionGroupName}}' with short name '{{shortName}}' and an Email receiver pointing to '{{emailAddress}}'.
Deploy a target Virtual Machine or App Service resource to monitor.
Create a Metric Alert rule named '{{alertRuleName}}' targeting the resource with condition 'Percentage CPU > {{thresholdPct}}'.
Attach '{{actionGroupName}}' to the alert rule with Severity {{severity}}.
Verify the alert rule status is enabled and inspect notification configuration.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Action Group
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Monitor** > in the left menu, select **Alerts** > click **Action groups** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{actionGroupName}}`, Display name: `{{shortName}}`. Under **Notifications**, Notification type: **Email/SMS message/Push/Voice**, Name: `EmailAdmin`, Email: `{{emailAddress}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.validation: az monitor action-group show --name {{actionGroupName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, ShortName:groupShortName}' -o table

steps.title: Deploy Test Compute Resource
steps.portalGuide: Deploy a lightweight VM `vm-alert-test` in `{{resourceGroup}}` (Ubuntu2204, Standard_B1s) to serve as the metric alert target.
steps.cliCommand:
az vm create \
  --name vm-alert-test \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --size Standard_B1s \
  --generate-ssh-keys

steps.title: Create Metric Alert Rule Linked to Action Group
steps.portalGuide: In **Monitor** > **Alerts** > click **+ Create** > **Alert rule**. Scope: select `vm-alert-test`. Condition: Signal name **Percentage CPU**, Operator: **Greater than**, Threshold: `{{thresholdPct}}`, Check every: `5 minutes`. Actions: Select existing action group `{{actionGroupName}}`. Details: Severity **{{severity}} - Warning**, Alert rule name: `{{alertRuleName}}` > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
VM_ID=$(az vm show --name vm-alert-test --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)
AG_ID=$(az monitor action-group show --name {{actionGroupName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)

az monitor metrics alert create \
  --name {{alertRuleName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --scopes "$VM_ID" \
  --condition "avg Percentage CPU > {{thresholdPct}}" \
  --window-size 5m \
  --evaluation-frequency 1m \
  --action "$AG_ID" \
  --severity {{severity}} \
  --description "Alert when CPU spikes above {{thresholdPct}}%"
steps.powershellCommand:
$vm = Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Name 'vm-alert-test'
$ag = Get-AzActionGroup -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Name '{{actionGroupName}}'
# Metric alert creation via PowerShell or Azure CLI
az monitor metrics alert show --name {{alertRuleName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}}
steps.validation: az monitor metrics alert show --name {{alertRuleName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, Severity:severity, Enabled:enabled}' -o table

title: Implement Azure Backup for Virtual Machines via Recovery Services Vault
summary: Protect virtual machine workloads using Azure Backup, configure customized backup policies with retention tiers, and trigger initial backup jobs.
scenarioTemplate: Business continuity and disaster recovery compliance at {{companyName}} mandates automated daily backups for IaaS workloads in '{{region}}'. You are tasked with creating resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provisioning an Azure Recovery Services Vault named '{{vaultName}}', creating a customized Backup Policy named '{{policyName}}' with {{snapshotDays}} days of instant recovery snapshot retention and {{dailyRetentionDays}} days of daily backup retention, and protecting a virtual machine.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy Azure Recovery Services Vault '{{vaultName}}' with storage redundancy set to LocallyRedundant (LRS).
Deploy a test Virtual Machine '{{vmName}}' in '{{resourceGroup}}'.
Configure an Azure Backup policy named '{{policyName}}' with daily frequency, {{snapshotDays}} days instant restore, and {{dailyRetentionDays}} days retention.
Enable backup on '{{vmName}}' referencing '{{policyName}}' and verify protection state.
Clean up all lab resources.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Recovery Services Vault
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Recovery Services vaults** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{vaultName}}`, Region: `{{region}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**. Once created, open `{{vaultName}}` > **Properties** > **Backup Configuration** > change Storage replication type to **Locally-redundant** > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az backup vault create \
  --name {{vaultName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}}

# Configure LRS storage redundancy:
az backup vault backup-properties set \
  --name {{vaultName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --backup-storage-redundancy LocallyRedundant

steps.title: Deploy Test Virtual Machine
steps.portalGuide: Deploy a lightweight VM `{{vmName}}` in `{{resourceGroup}}` (Ubuntu2204, Standard_B1s).

steps.title: Enable Backup and Configure Protection Policy
steps.portalGuide: In `{{vaultName}}`, select **Overview** > **+ Backup**. Workload: **Azure**, What do you want to backup: **Virtual machine** > click **Backup**. Policy: Create new `{{policyName}}` (Daily 23:00, Instant restore {{snapshotDays}} days, Retention {{dailyRetentionDays}} days). Virtual Machines: Select `{{vmName}}` > click **Enable backup**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Enable backup on VM:
az backup protection enable-for-vm \
  --vault-name {{vaultName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --vm $(az vm show --name {{vmName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv) \
  --policy-name DefaultPolicy
steps.validation: az backup container list --vault-name {{vaultName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --backup-management-type AzureIaasVM --query "[].{Name:name, Status:properties.registrationStatus}" -o table

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: In `{{vaultName}}` > **Backup items** > select VM > **Stop backup** > **Delete backup data**. Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand:
# Stop protection and delete backup data:
az backup protection disable \
  --vault-name {{vaultName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --container-name {{vmName}} \
  --item-name {{vmName}} \
  --delete-backup-data true --yes 2>/dev/null || true

az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait

title: Troubleshoot Network Connectivity using Azure Network Watcher
summary: Diagnose network connectivity issues, verify NSG traffic filtering using IP Flow Verify, and inspect routing with Next Hop analysis.
scenarioTemplate: Users report that application servers in '{{region}}' are unable to communicate with an external API at '{{targetIp}}' on port {{targetPort}}. You must utilize Azure Network Watcher in '{{region}}' to diagnose the failure. Using **IP Flow Verify**, determine whether inbound or outbound NSG security rules are dropping packets. Then run **Next Hop** analysis on Virtual Machine '{{vmName}}' to confirm whether traffic routes via VirtualAppliance, VirtualNetwork, or Internet.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify Azure Network Watcher is enabled for region '{{region}}'.
Deploy Virtual Machine '{{vmName}}' in '{{resourceGroup}}'.
Execute Network Watcher IP Flow Verify test on '{{vmName}}' targeting IP '{{targetIp}}' on port {{targetPort}}.
Execute Network Watcher Next Hop analysis from '{{vmName}}' to target IP '{{targetIp}}'.
Interpret results (Access Allowed / Denied and effective security rule name).
Clean up all lab resources.

steps.title: Verify Network Watcher and Create Test VM
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Network Watcher**. Verify your target region `{{region}}` status is **Enabled**. Create RG `{{resourceGroup}}` and deploy VM `{{vmName}}` (Ubuntu2204, Standard_B1s) with a virtual network.
steps.cliCommand:
# Ensure Network Watcher is enabled for region:
az network watcher configure \
  --locations {{region}} \
  --enabled true \
  --resource-group NetworkWatcherRG 2>/dev/null || true

az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az vm create \
  --name {{vmName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --size Standard_B1s \
  --generate-ssh-keys
steps.validation: az network watcher list --query "[?location=='{{region}}'].{Location:location, Provisioning:provisioningState}" -o table

steps.title: Run IP Flow Verify to Inspect NSG Rule Evaluation
steps.portalGuide: In **Network Watcher**, select **IP flow verify** (under Network diagnostic tools). Target: `{{vmName}}`, Protocol: `{{protocol}}`, Direction: **Outbound**, Local IP: (VM IP), Local port: `*`, Remote IP: `{{targetIp}}`, Remote port: `{{targetPort}}` > click **Check**. Observe whether the result is **Access Allowed** or **Access Denied**, and view the matching NSG security rule.
steps.cliCommand:
VM_NIC_ID=$(az vm show --name {{vmName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'networkProfile.networkInterfaces[0].id' -o tsv)

az network watcher test-ip-flow \
  --vm {{vmName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --direction Outbound \
  --protocol {{protocol}} \
  --local 10.0.0.4:* \
  --remote {{targetIp}}:{{targetPort}}

steps.title: Run Next Hop Analysis for Route Diagnostics
steps.portalGuide: In **Network Watcher**, select **Next hop** (under Network diagnostic tools). Target: `{{vmName}}`, Source IP: (VM IP), Destination IP: `{{targetIp}}` > click **Next hop**. Inspect whether the next hop is **Internet**, **VirtualAppliance**, or **VirtualNetwork**.
